prompt.context: Tristar is a large international manufacturer of electronics, home appliances, software, and biotech products. Their home appliance line (refrigerators, washers & dryers, microwaves) has been very successful in the United States, mostly through a B2C model: they get their products into retailers like Best Buy, Sears, Home Depot, etc. Tristar management has set aggressive revenue targets for the coming year, and the home appliance business unit director has some concerns about meeting them. She has asked your firm for help in evaluating a new opportunity: B2B sales, specifically the home builders market. Tristar would sell appliances to builders, who would then install them in their new units. Sales could also occur for home remodeling.
prompt.question: Should Tristar enter the home builders market, and can this new channel help close the gap between their revenue targets and projections?

clarifying_info.q: Who are Tristar's current competitors in the builders market?
clarifying_info.a: The builders market is split 50/50 between two competitors: GE and Whirlpool.

clarifying_info.q: Does Tristar have existing distribution in the builders market?
clarifying_info.a: Tristar has strong sales throughout the US via retail, but in the builders market deliveries must occur on a particular day to a particular building site — this is fundamentally different from supplying inventory to a retailer like Best Buy.

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue targets vs. current projections?
clarifying_info.a: You will share that information via an exhibit shortly.

exhibits.title: Retail Sales Opportunity
exhibits.shows: A table comparing Total Revenue Opportunity, Tristar Target (~30% market share), and Tristar Expected 2017 Sales across multiple retailers and in total.

exhibits.title: Builders Market Data
exhibits.shows: New home price and cost breakdown, plus expected appliance spend per remodeling project by project type (Single Family and Multi-Family, Minor/Major/New Addition).

exhibits.title: Distribution Channels
exhibits.shows: A diagram of distribution channels in the home builders market showing Manufacturer, Large Distributors, Small Builder/Distributors, Large Builder/Distributors, and Large Builders. Existing Tristar relationships are indicated.

exhibits.title: Distribution Market Share
exhibits.shows: A chart showing the market share breakdown among distributors and builders in the home builders market.

framework: Revenues: Assess the volume (new home starts, remodeling projects) and pricing (appliance spend per unit) to size the builders market and estimate potential revenue
Company capabilities: Evaluate production capacity and distribution capacity to serve the builders market's time/site-specific delivery requirements
Competition: Analyze current market concentration (GE and Whirlpool hold 50/50 share); estimate realistic share Tristar could capture and anticipate competitive response
Costs: Acknowledge that new distribution infrastructure will require upfront investment and incremental administration (secondary to revenue analysis in this case)
Risks: Assess housing market cyclicality and risk of diverting management attention from core retail business

questions.prompt: Step 1 (Exhibit 1): What is the revenue gap between Tristar's target and expected 2017 retail sales? Can this gap be closed through the existing retail channel?
questions.guidance: Candidate should subtract expected sales from target to identify the gap. Should note that growing from ~23% to ~30% market share is very ambitious given market saturation, making it unlikely the gap can be closed through retail alone — the B2B builders opportunity must be explored.

math.setup: Gap = Tristar Target - Tristar Expected 2017 Sales
math.answer: Approximately $1.1 billion gap. Reaching 30% share from ~23% is ambitious; retail alone cannot close the gap.

questions.prompt: Step 2 (Exhibit 2): Calculate the size of the home builders market — both new homes and remodeling segments.
questions.guidance: Candidate should work through new home construction math step by step: back out margin/land/other costs to get construction cost, apply 2% appliance rate, multiply by ~1M annual new home starts. Then sum the remodeling table row by row. Should highlight that remodeling ($7.6B) exceeds new homes ($4.2B), and the combined $11.8B market means only ~10% share is needed to close the gap.

math.setup:
New homes: Average price $300,000. Non-construction deductions = builder margin 6% + land 15% + other 10% = 31%, so construction costs = 69% ~ 70% of price. Appliances = 2% of construction costs. Use ~1M new home starts/year.
Remodeling: For each row, multiply (number of projects in thousands) x (% purchasing appliances) x (average spend per project).
steps: 10% of $11.8B = $1.18B — sufficient to close the ~$1.1B gap
math.answer: New homes: $4.2B; Remodeling: $7.6B; Total: $11.8B. Capturing ~10% of this market closes the revenue gap.

questions.prompt: Step 3 (Exhibit 3): What distribution channels are available to Tristar in the home builders market, and what are the key strategic considerations?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize: (1) Tristar already has relationships with Large Distributors who serve both small and large Builder/Distributors — this is the lower-investment entry path. (2) Tristar could build direct relationships with Builder/Distributors to capture more value. (3) Reaching Large Builders directly is possible but requires a fundamentally different, capital-intensive distribution setup. Key insight: the builders model requires day/site-specific delivery vs. bulk retailer replenishment — a real operational challenge.

questions.prompt: Step 4 (Exhibit 4): Given the distribution market share data, which channel segment should Tristar prioritize to hit its 10% share target?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that Builder/Distributors account for approximately 80% of the market. Targeting this segment — leverageable through Tristar's existing Large Distributor relationships — is the most capital-efficient path to achieving 10% overall share. Pursuing Large Builders directly is possible but requires a separate, more costly distribution infrastructure.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors and considerations will determine the feasibility of Tristar entering the home builders market?

categories.name: Distribution
ideas: New time/site-specific delivery model required — fundamentally different from bulk retailer replenishment
Leverage existing Large Distributor relationships as the lowest-cost entry path
Potential to build direct relationships with Builder/Distributors for higher margin capture
Logistics investment needed for last-mile delivery to job sites

categories.name: Competition
ideas: Market currently concentrated: GE and Whirlpool hold 50/50 share
Tristar is comparable in scale — credible threat to incumbents
Risk of price cuts or exclusive agreements from incumbents defending share
Strategic choice of which geographies or segments to enter first

categories.name: Capacity
ideas: Production capacity to handle incremental B2B volume
Logistics and distribution capacity for builders delivery model
Administrative and sales force capacity for B2B contract management

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Determine whether Tristar must discount to win builders contracts
Volume/long-term contracts may offset lower unit prices with revenue stability
Pricing strategy may vary between large builders (scale discounts) and small builders

categories.name: Market risks
ideas: Housing market cyclicality — new home starts can drop sharply in downturns
Remodeling market is larger and likely more recession-resilient
Risk of management distraction from core retail business

recommendation: Tristar should pursue entry into the home builders market as the primary lever to close the ~$1.1B revenue gap
The combined builders market ($11.8B) is large; Tristar needs only ~10% share, and is competitively sized vs. GE and Whirlpool to achieve this
risks: Upfront investment required to build a new distribution model capable of time/site-specific delivery
Housing market volatility makes new-home-starts revenue less predictable
Risk of diverting management attention and capital from the core retail business
next_steps: Study the competitive landscape to identify which geographic markets to attack first and how to price competitively
Conduct in-depth distribution channel analysis to map the fastest path to establishing direct relationships with Builder/Distributors
Assess production and logistics capacity requirements to serve the builders segment at target volume
